CASEY CAGLE.name: L.S. "Casey" Cagle
CASEY CAGLE.background: Lowell Stacy "Casey" Cagle, Republican, born Jan. 12, 1966 in Gainesville, Ga.; raised by a single mother; seventh-generation Hall County resident. Johnson High School; attended Georgia Southern University (football) and Gainesville State College. Built a tuxedo rental business from 1986; founded Southern Heritage Bank in 1999 and chaired it until its 2004 merger into Gainesville Bank & Trust. Georgia State Senate, District 49, elected 1994 (defeating Democratic incumbent Jane Hemmer; youngest member), chaired Senate Finance. Lieutenant governor Jan. 8, 2007 - Jan. 14, 2019, Georgia's first Republican in the office; re-elected 2010 and 2014. Withdrew from the 2010 governor's race on April 15, 2009, citing a degenerative spinal condition.
CASEY CAGLE.ideology: Wikipedia (summarizing coverage) says that in the 2018 governor's race he appealed to the party's right flank, presented himself as a strong Trump supporter and attacked the media as "fake news"; it notes the AJC said his effort to portray himself as a fiscal conservative was undercut by his taxpayer-funded air travel. In 2018 he described himself as "the No. 2 guy" with 12 years' experience in budgeting and policy negotiation (Atlanta Jewish Times).
CASEY CAGLE.record: As lieutenant governor, supported the Republican plan cutting the top individual and corporate income tax rate (to 5.75% in 2019 and 5.5% in 2020) and doubling the standard deduction. After Delta Air Lines ended its NRA discount in February 2018, he said on Feb. 26, 2018 he would block tax legislation benefiting Delta; the General Assembly then dropped a jet-fuel tax break. Created the College and Career Academies. In 2018, recordings released by former candidate Clay Tippins captured him saying he backed "bad public policy" to hurt Hunter Hill's campaign; a New York Times report examined a 2008 condo purchase from a gas lobbyist below appraisal, and an AJC investigation found about $265,000 in taxpayer-funded air travel 2010-2018. Finished first in the May 22, 2018 Republican primary for governor (39.0%) and lost the July 24 runoff to Brian Kemp (30.5% per the official results).
CASEY CAGLE.notes: Rechecked 2026-11-05: rebuilt from Wikipedia, WABE and Atlanta Jewish Times; Wikipedia gives the runoff as 69%-30%; Wikipedia infobox/body disagree on whether his Senate service ended in 2006 or 2007. positions.stance: Pledged 500,000 new jobs in his first four years as governor, through expanding existing businesses, recruiting companies from other states and startup incubators at regional universities; zero-based budgeting.

"Being a low-tax state is important to our prosperity"; cited the cut in the income tax rate from 6% to 5.5% and said it could be lowered further; proposed lowering income taxes for individuals and small businesses by adjusting exemptions and deductions.

Called for a "war on dropouts"; wanted to expand the College and Career Academies he created as lieutenant governor so every high schooler has access, plus more apprenticeships; led the raise of the private-school scholarship tax credit cap (HB 217) from $58 million to $100 million.
Supported the 2016 religious-liberty bill Gov. Deal vetoed; said he would sign religious liberty legislation matching federal law, while saying "I am not for discrimination in any way or any form."

Backed the 2016 law barring state business with entities that boycott Israel and SB 356 on the Georgia Commission on the Holocaust; "We do not condone businesses and others that hold a grudge toward Israel."
Opposed the approach of the unsuccessful 2018 hate-crimes bill but said he was open to ways to be more sensitive on the issue.
Overhaul state planning for road and infrastructure maintenance; infrastructure investment beyond roads and bridges.

orig.background: Born and raised in Georgia. Undergraduate degree from Georgia State University; graduate degree from Clayton State University. Henry County Commissioner for District 4 from 2017 to March 2024, and vice chair of the Board of Commissioners in 2022. Resigned in 2024 to run for county chair and lost that primary to incumbent Carlotta Harrell. Ran as a Democrat in the Nov. 5, 2024 special election to reclaim District 4 and finished second (24.4%), forcing a runoff. Lost the Dec. 3, 2024 runoff to interim Commissioner Michael Price, 35.8% to 64.1%. Grandmother of Stockbridge Mayor-elect Jayden Williams.

WESLEY BEAMON.name: Wesley Beamon
WESLEY BEAMON.background: Sumter County native living in Americus with his wife, Deanna. A.S. health studies, Central Georgia Technical College; B.S. fire science administration, Waldorf University; J.D. Mercer University. Six years in the U.S. Marine Corps (sergeant); former firefighter-paramedic with Americus Fire and Emergency Services and volunteer with the Schley County Fire Department. Founder of Beamon Law, LLC (criminal and DUI defense); certified mediator and arbitrator; contract public defender in Sumter County State Court and Lee County Probate Court; Schley County magistrate judge since 2017.
WESLEY BEAMON.record: Ran on May 19, 2026 for the Southwestern Circuit (Lee, Macon, Schley, Stewart, Sumter, Webster counties) Superior Court seat of retiring Judge W. James Sizemore Jr. and did not win (26.2%).

Branch lists: B.A., Augusta College; J.D., Widener University School of Law; assistant district attorney, Augusta Circuit 1996-2003; adjunct criminal justice professor, Troy University 2001-2010; juvenile court judge 2007-2012 and later chief juvenile judge; also public defender and private practice.
